samples.summary: A pre-existing straddling merge makes every row/column reorder impossible, not just the ones that create the straddle
samples.evidence: `moveCells` builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(...)` and refuses if ANY resulting block crosses the freeze: `for (const [anchorSref, span] of movedMerges) { if (this.crossesFreezePane(...)) { this.refuse('merge-move-frozen'); return false; } }`. The check is on the post-move map as a whole, not on whether the move *introduced* the straddle. A block that already straddles the boundary (reachable today: `Sheet.setFreezePane` did not snap before this change, `loadFreezePane`/`loadMerges` still do not snap on load — sheet.ts:567-591 — and `worksheet-shape-migration.ts:449` and `seed-templates.ts:140` can write freeze+merges independently) maps to itself under `moveMergeMap`, so it still crosses afterwards. The result: every reorder of completely unrelated rows or columns is refused with "Can't move a merged cell across a frozen row or column", permanently, until the user unfreezes or unmerges. The same shape exists on the API (`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`, worksheet-structure.controller.ts:194-203), where it yields a permanent 409 on `POST move` for such a document.

samples.summary: API `POST move` returns 409 forever on a document that already contains a merge across the freeze
samples.evidence: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` iterates the whole moved merge map and throws `ConflictException` for any block crossing the boundary, including blocks whose straddling state predates the request and is unchanged by it (`moveMergeMap` is identity for a block outside the moved span, and is also identity for a no-op move where `dstIndex` falls inside `[srcIndex, srcIndex+count]`). Since the only repair paths are `PUT freeze`, `POST insert` and `POST delete`, a caller that only wants to reorder rows has no way to proceed and gets a 409 with a message naming an unrelated merge anchor.

samples.summary: The freeze snap is unbounded, so a tall/wide merged block can set frozenRows/Cols to a value the renderer paints row-by-row every frame
samples.evidence: `setFreezePane` now stores `snapFreezePastMerges(...)` with no ceiling on the result. The merge budget permits a single span of `MaxMergedCells = 100000` cells (e.g. `rs: 100000, cs: 1`), so freezing row 1 under such a block snaps `frozenRows` to 100000. `GridCanvas.render` then calls `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` for quadrants A and B (gridcanvas.ts:329-352, 400-403), and `buildRenderableRefs(rowStart, rowEnd, ...)` materializes one ref per frozen cell — the clip rect does not bound the loop. That is exactly the pathology `parseFreeze`'s own doc comment describes ("an out-of-grid freeze allocates per frame and the UI never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it"), now reachable from a normal editor gesture (freeze 1 row) and from `PUT freeze` with a modest `rows` value. `snapFreezePastMerges` should clamp, or the gesture should be refused rather than snapped, past some bound.

samples.summary: `revalidateCopyBuffer` silently no-ops when the copied range had no axis IDs, leaving a stale buffer after a peer's structural edit
samples.evidence: `if (!buffer?.sourceAnchors) return;` — and `anchorsForRange` returns undefined whenever either corner is past axis-ID coverage (`refToAnchor` returns null for `rowOrder[ref.r - 1] === undefined`). `rowOrder` starts empty (`createWorksheet`, worksheet-document.ts:145) and grows lazily, so a copy whose range extends past covered rows/columns records no anchors. For such a buffer a remote insert/delete/reorder never drops it, and the next paste is still treated as internal: `relocateGrid` and the new `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges` then write cells and re-create merged blocks at coordinates that no longer mean what they did at copy time. The no-op is the opposite of the safe default for a validity check.

samples.summary: A copy's merge snapshot is never revalidated, so a paste can re-create a merged block the user has since unmerged
samples.evidence: `const sourceDrops = isCut ? this.liveMergesAmong(sourceMerges) : [];` — `liveMergesAmong` (the guard that checks the recorded block still exists with the same span) is applied only on the cut path. `plan.pasted` is built unconditionally from `sourceMerges`, the snapshot taken at copy time. Sequence: copy a merged A1:B1, unmerge A1:B1, paste at A3 — a merged block reappears at A3:B3 even though no such block exists anywhere on the sheet, and `clearCellsUnderMerge` then deletes the content of B3. Combined with the view no longer calling `clearCopyBuffer` after each paste (view/worksheet.ts, view/spreadsheet.ts), the stale snapshot now survives arbitrarily long. The docstring claims this is intentional clipboard semantics, but the cell-clearing side effect makes it a silent content loss rather than a layout choice.

verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim: moveCells (sheet.ts:1566-1572) checks the whole post-move merge map with crossesFreezePane rather than checking whether the move introduced the straddle, and moveMerge/moveMergeMap (merging.ts:200-273) map an untouched block to itself, so a pre-existing straddling block trips the refusal for any reorder of unrelated rows/columns. The straddling state is reachable and unguarded on the move path: loadFreezePane/loadMerges do not snap (sheet.ts:567-591), the legacy shape migration copies merges and freeze wholesale (worksheet-shape-migration.ts:444-450), and the repo's own test seeds exactly this state through the store/load path (merge.test.ts:942-954) while the design doc notes such a block is only 'healed by the first structural edit' (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:126-129) — shiftCells snaps (sheet.ts:1431-1442) but moveCells never does. The same shape yields a permanent 409 on the API (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:181-204). Real correctness bug on a reachable path; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: API `POST move` returns 409 forever on a document that already contains a merge across the freeze
finding.evidence: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` iterates the whole moved merge map and throws `ConflictException` for any block crossing the boundary, including blocks whose straddling state predates the request and is unchanged by it (`moveMergeMap` is identity for a block outside the moved span, and is also identity for a no-op move where `dstIndex` falls inside `[srcIndex, srcIndex+count]`). Since the only repair paths are `PUT freeze`, `POST insert` and `POST delete`, a caller that only wants to reorder rows has no way to proceed and gets a 409 with a message naming an unrelated merge anchor.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:181-204 walks the entire moved merge map and 409s on any straddler, including one unchanged by the move), but it is not a blocking correctness defect. (a) The triggering state — a merge straddling a freeze — is prevented at every writer in the repo: PUT merges 409s (worksheet.controller.ts:193-209), PUT freeze snaps (worksheet.controller.ts:121-128), insert/delete snap the line past the block (worksheet-structure.ts:271-288, tested at worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:504-546), and the editor refuses merge/paste/drag-move (sheet.ts:4881, 2614, 2881); the XLSX importer writes merges but never writes freeze. (b) The check is a faithful mirror of the engine's own refusal in Sheet.moveCells (sheet.ts:1554-1572), so the API is consistent rather than wrong. (c) The reviewer's impact premise is false: PUT freeze accepts 0 (snapFreezePastMerges returns line unchanged when line <= 0, merging.ts:329) and insert/delete repair by snapping, and the 409 message itself names the repair. (d) The no-op sub-case is already rejected with 400 upstream when dstIndex falls inside the moved block (backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts:306-311). (e) The throw precedes applyWorksheetMove inside doc.update, so nothing is partially written. That grades as minor under this lens (defensive branch on an already-invariant-violating document, failing loudly with a documented repair), not major/blocking.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. sheet.ts:543-548 stores the snapped value unconditionally; merging.ts:324-336 only grows the line and never clamps it; mergeBudgetAdmits (merging.ts:86-100) permits a single {rs:100000, cs:1} span, which canMergeSelection (sheet.ts:4891) and PUT merges both accept, so freezing row 1 under it snaps frozenRows to 100000. gridcanvas.ts:329-332 and :400-405 then call renderQuadrantCells with rowStart=1, rowEnd=fr+1 for quadrants B and A; the surrounding ctx.clip() (320-328, 396-399) bounds painting, not iteration, and buildRenderableRefs (gridcanvas.ts:856-878, invoked at :609 each frame) allocates a Ref plus a toSref string per frozen cell, with buildTextOverflowRenderData (:598-608) walking the same range. No clamp exists on any path: view/worksheet.ts:467-474 forwards unchanged, layout.ts:136-153 copies frozenRows through, and worksheet.controller.ts:121-128 writes the snapped result without re-checking parseFreeze's grid bound — the very bound whose doc comment (worksheet-settings.ts:53-56) describes this per-frame-allocation/UI-never-paints pathology. This is a correctness-lane resource/state defect (an invariant the renderer relies on, broken by a reachable normal gesture, leaving the UI unable to paint or to reach the menu that would undo it), not a style or design concern, so no refutation ground applies.
